title: Plagiarisation of "Count On Me Singapore" Song and Actions against Infringements of National Symbols
what_it_is: Plagiarisation of "Count On Me Singapore" Song and Actions against Infringements of National Symbols

sections.label: Questions on national song copyright
sections.summary: Questions ask what actions protect Singapore's copyright and the Government's stance on infringing national symbols and songs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) with regard to the case of an Indian composer plagiarising the song titled "Count on Me Singapore", what actions has the Ministry taken to protect Singapore's copyright; and (b) what is the policy stance of the Government towards individuals who infringe on Singapore's national symbols and songs, whether for commercial gain or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether the Ministry regularly checks the media and the Internet for possible infringements of our national symbols; (b) how many cases of copyright infringement have been uncovered to date and how were they dealt with; and (c) whether there are any plans to enhance the protection of intellectual property rights for our national symbols.

sections.label: Mendoza withdraws claims to song
sections.summary: Mr Mendoza admitted having no evidence, withdrew all claims to the song, and confirmed rights remain with Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In response to our requests for proof of his claims and to substantiate his position, Mr Mendoza then changed his position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He admitted that he had no evidence to support his claims and confirmed the following in writing:  (a) that he unconditionally and irrevocably withdraws all claims to the lyrics and music of the song, "We Can Achieve" which he recognises is similar to "Count on Me, Singapore";  (b) that he had informed all his associates and networks of the above and also instructed all social media platforms to pull down the song "We can Achieve" with immediate effect; and  (c) that he had no intention of attacking the integrity or professionalism of Mr Harrison, the original composer of "Count on Me, Singapore".

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Mendoza's admission leaves no doubt that "Count on Me, Singapore" was written by Mr Harrison and that the rights and ownership in the national song remain with us.

sections.label: MCCY protects national songs symbols
sections.summary: MCCY takes challenges to proprietary rights in national songs and symbols seriously and will take necessary steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) takes any challenge to our proprietary rights and interests in our national songs and symbols very seriously, and we will take the necessary steps to protect them.

sections.label: Government holds third-party song copyright
sections.summary: Most songs written by third parties have their copyright held by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As for Mr Giam's first question, most of the songs which were written by third parties, the copyright is with the Government.

sections.label: Mendoza admitted no ownership interest
sections.summary: Mr Mendoza admitted he has no ownership interest and no evidence to substantiate his claim to the song.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I explained earlier, Mr Mendoza did in fact admit that he has no ownership interest; he has got no evidence to substantiate his position that he lays any claim to the song.

sections.label: Asserting rights without legal action
sections.summary: Asserting rights need not mean legal action; persuading Mr Mendoza to withdraw his claims was more efficient and effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Leong should not also confuse asserting our rights with necessarily taking legal action, legal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And in this case, it was far more efficient, quicker and a lot more effective for Mr Mendoza to be persuaded that his own position was untenable, for his claims to be withdrawn by himself and not in any way removing the Singapore Government's claim and, in fact, for all Singaporeans' interest in the songs to be preserved.
